scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and automatically fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills (CL-01).
symptoms: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05).
Majority (~59%) of disputed bills used ACTUAL meter reads rather than ESTIMATED substitutes, contrary to what a pure estimate-substitution cause would predict (E-01).
Field manual-read route completion in Aug-Sep ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target, affecting 9,200 manual-read accounts (E-03).
Dispute ticket response times remain within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target), so backlog/response speed is not the pain point (E-04).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from a ~600/month baseline (Jun/Jul) to 1,180-1,260/month (Aug/Sep) (E-05), driven by a defect in billing import validation rules that misclassifies/corrupts meter reads during import — producing incorrect bills across both ACTUAL and ESTIMATED read types (E-01 shows ACTUAL reads are the majority, ~59%, of disputed bills, ruling out estimate-substitution as the dominant cause) — while tariff-rate changes are ruled out as a cause (E-02 shows zero logged tariff changes, corroborated by E-06).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-01 revised by E-12: re-read under E-12 (accepted premise check) — PR-ROOT: E-12's confirmed REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejection mechanism exactly matches the 1,240 ESTIMATED-type disputes (E-01) but gives zero evidence that the same defect also produces the 1,785 ACTUAL-type disputes (59%, the stated majority) the root problem claims it covers.; PR-CHAIN-2: The confirmed mechanism (valid AMI read rejected -> estimate used) explains precisely the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes but is unaddressed/unconfirmed for the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes that make up the claimed majority driver of this chain step.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-capacity problem, solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets, independent of why bills are actually wrong.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to the billing import validation rules around August caused reads or estimates to be misclassified, producing incorrect bills and the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: The MDMS nightly export of AMI reads (H-MDMS-BILL) began failing or degrading since August, forcing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter-read completion (contracted via ORG-FIELD) dropped since August, increasing missed reads and estimate substitutions that generated wrong bills.

H-HANDOFF-SEMANTIC-MISMATCH.statement: A semantic/format defect in one of the data handoffs (H-FIELD-BILL or H-MDMS-BILL) into billing import is silently corrupting read values independent of rule changes, vendor outages, or staffing.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule flags/rejects AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, discarding 1,184 valid pre-cutoff AMI reads for disputed/estimated accounts despite successful export, independent of tariff or field-staffing causes (E-12).

H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH.statement: AMI meters with firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06) report consumption in register_unit '0.1 m3' instead of whole 'm3' used by legacy v3.x meters; if billing import fails to convert this unit scale, v4.2 reads appear ~10x inflated, both triggering spurious REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rejections (E-12) and potentially inflating bills built on ACTUAL v4.2 reads that are not rejected.

No pre-August baseline is given, so this does not by itself establish that completion dropped since August versus a pre-existing gap.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, interview) claims the field-reading team has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers' accounts to fall to estimated bills. This offers a candidate causal mechanism for E-03's observed Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (0.88 vs 0.95 target), but SH-FIELD has a stated incentive toward headcount increase and a bias to attribute problems to staffing, so it needs independent corroboration.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is a contract clause confirming that route priority change requests by the utility must be executed only after Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation; it documents the authorization basis already reflected in constraint K-DISPATCH and does not speak to the billing-dispute causal mechanism.

E-09.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: 320 accounts received estimated bills in the last billing cycle, spread across 40 routes (billing-db, E-09). That volume is far smaller than the 9,200 manual-read accounts affected by the Aug-Sep route completion shortfall (E-03) and the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-01), indicating only a small fraction of lagging routes actually convert to estimated bills.

E-10.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query (E-10, AUTHORITATIVE/COMPLETE) identifies 14 specific routes with below-target completion (sample: 0.70 for R-00), giving route-level detail behind the aggregate Aug-Sep shortfall (E-03) from a tool source independent of SH-FIELD's self-interested interview (E-07). E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder) reports that vendor-side MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned (vendor ticket TX-4471), which, if true, would remove the access blocker that previously made querying DA-MDMS infeasible (ACCESS_PENDING / mdms-export DEGRADED). This is a logistics/access claim, not evidence about AMI read content or the dispute root cause itself.

E-12 (MDMS export, now accessible) shows that of AMI reads tied to disputed/estimated accounts, 1,184 were received before cutoff and exported to billing but tagged billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 show NO_READ_RECEIVED. This points to a billing-import validation rule rejecting valid AMI reads on a high-consumption trigger as a concrete mechanism, rather than AMI delivery/vendor outage, and resolves the MDMS access blocker.

MDMS firmware/register-unit data shows firmware v4.2 (rolled out 2026-06, before the August dispute surge) reports consumption in units of '0.1 m3' while legacy firmware v3.x reports in whole 'm3'. If billing import does not convert v4.2's scaled units, v4.2 reads would appear roughly 10x inflated, offering a mechanism that could both trigger the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION rule seen in E-12 and potentially inflate consumption on ACTUAL-type bills that pass through unrejected.

E-14.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-config's validation_rule_changes log directly confirms rule BV-17, a high-consumption check comparing raw register value with 12-month m3 history, was deployed 2026-08-01 with unit_scaling="none"; the only other change (BV-09, label text) is irrelevant. This is the first direct billing-config evidence of a rule change timed with the dispute surge, and its lack of unit scaling is exactly the mechanism that would make v4.2 firmware's 0.1 m3-scaled raw register reads (E-13) appear ~10x inflated against m3-based history, triggering the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcome seen in E-12.

U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.question: Has a specific billing import validation rule actually changed around August, and what is the exact defect misclassifying reads/estimates?
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.decision_impact: Confirms or disconfirms the entire causal mechanism the problem rests on; without it, remediation targeting billing-config could be misdirected.
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.resolution_path: Query the billing-config rule change log for entries dated around August and correlate timing/content with the disputed-bill read-type pattern (E-01).
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.safe_placeholder: Treat H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE as the working diagnostic hypothesis only; take no corrective action until the specific defect is identified in billing-config.
U-RULE-DEFECT-CONFIRM.resolution: E-12's billing_import_status field directly surfaces a candidate defect mechanism (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION discarding 1,184 valid AMI reads); this corroborates but does not substitute for a direct billing-config (DA-RULES) rule-change log entry confirming timing, which remains unconfirmed.

U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.question: What do AMI read events (DA-MDMS) show for disputed accounts, and does this corroborate or rule out an AMI-side contribution, given vendor export access is ACCESS_PENDING and mdms-export is DEGRADED?
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.decision_impact: Without MDMS data, an AMI-side contribution to the misclassification cannot be ruled in or out, limiting confidence in the final diagnosis.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution_path: Await ORG-AMI vendor provisioning of mdms-export access; retry query_mdms_read_events once access is restored.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-rule and read-type diagnosis using billing-db/billing-config only; exclude AMI-side data from the diagnosis conclusion until mdms-export access is granted.
U-MDMS-ACCESS-PENDING.resolution: MDMS export access was provisioned and the query succeeded (E-12): the AMI-side contribution is dominated by billing-import rejection of valid reads (1,184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) rather than non-delivery (only 56 NO_READ_RECEIVED), resolving the access-pending blocker.

U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.question: Does an independent, authoritative source corroborate SH-FIELD's claim of a reader shortage since July, beyond the biased stakeholder interview (E-07)?
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.decision_impact: Determines whether field staffing should be elevated from a secondary assumption to an active contributor requiring its own remediation track.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.resolution_path: Cross-check E-07 against an authoritative, non-stakeholder source such as route-log historical trends or field services contract staffing records.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.safe_placeholder: Keep A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-MINOR as the working assumption and do not redirect remediation effort toward field staffing until corroborated.
U-FIELD-SHORTAGE-CORROBORATION.resolution: route-log (E-10) independently identifies 14 specific lagging routes with sub-target completion, providing authoritative tool-level corroboration of a route completion shortfall distinct from SH-FIELD's interview claim, though it still does not confirm reader staffing shortage as the specific cause.

U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.question: Does the CRM ticket-volume metric distinguish billing-error disputes from other dispute reasons, so a drop in raw ticket count reliably reflects bill-correctness improvement?
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.decision_impact: Affects whether M-DISPUTE-VOL alone is a valid success signal or needs a reason-coded sub-metric.
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.resolution_path: Check crm-tickets for a dispute-reason field distinguishing billing-error disputes from other reasons.
U-TICKET-REASON-TAGGING.safe_placeholder: Treat M-DISPUTE-VOL as a volume proxy only, flagging that a drop may include non-billing-reason tickets until reason tagging is confirmed.

U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.question: Does the same BV-17/firmware-v4.2 unit-scaling defect (via inflated-but-not-rejected v4.2 reads) or a separate mechanism explain the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills?
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.decision_impact: Determines whether the confirmed BV-17 fix fully resolves the dispute surge or only the ESTIMATED-read minority, which changes release scope and claimed impact.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.resolution_path: Join disputed ACTUAL-read bills (billing-db) against meter firmware/register-unit data (mdms-export) to test whether v4.2 unit inflation also appears, unrejected, in ACTUAL-read bills.
U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM.safe_placeholder: Ship the diagnosis scoped only to the confirmed ESTIMATED-read/BV-17 mechanism; do not claim the remedy explains the ACTUAL-read majority until this is resolved.

U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-RESIDUAL.question: Does field route-completion lag (E-03, E-10) still contribute an independent residual share of disputes alongside the BV-17 defect, given only 320 accounts actually converted to estimated bills last cycle (E-09) versus 1,240 ESTIMATED disputes?
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-RESIDUAL.decision_impact: Determines whether field-route corroboration work is needed as a secondary remediation track or can be deprioritized.
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-RESIDUAL.resolution_path: Cross-reference the 320 estimated-bill accounts (E-09) against disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-01) to measure the residual share not explained by BV-17.
U-FIELD-CONTRIBUTION-RESIDUAL.safe_placeholder: Treat field-route lag as a secondary, unconfirmed contributor and exclude it from the primary remediation scope pending corroboration.

U-DEFECT-SCOPE-BEYOND-DISPUTED.question: Does the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 unit-scaling defect also silently affect v4.2-meter accounts that have not yet filed a dispute?
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-BEYOND-DISPUTED.decision_impact: Affects whether remediation must be proactive across all v4.2 accounts or can be limited to the already-disputed population.
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-BEYOND-DISPUTED.resolution_path: Query billing-db for v4.2-meter accounts with no filed dispute and check whether their bills show the same unexplained high-consumption or rejection pattern.
U-DEFECT-SCOPE-BEYOND-DISPUTED.safe_placeholder: Report the defect scope as limited to disputed accounts and flag non-disputed v4.2 accounts as an open monitoring item rather than asserting they are unaffected.

U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.question: Is the nightly H-MDMS-BILL export (AMI register reads, ORG-AMI to ORG-UTIL) delivering complete, semantically valid data into billing import, independent of the diagnostic mdms-export tool query already used in E-12?
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.decision_impact: A residual handoff-level corruption, if present, would need separate remediation from the BV-17 rule fix even though E-12 already rules it out as the dominant driver.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Verify H-MDMS-BILL's nightly export delivery_status and semantic_validity directly against ORG-AMI delivery logs, separate from the mdms-export diagnostic query.
U-MDMS-HANDOFF-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Rely on the confirmed BV-17/firmware mechanism (E-12, E-14) as the primary explanation; treat any residual handoff-level corruption as a separate, not-yet-ruled-out contributor.

A-RULE-CHANGE-UNCONFIRMED.statement: The specific billing import validation rule change/defect has not been directly observed in billing-config; H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE's support rests on eliminating tariff and estimate-substitution explanations rather than a direct observation of a rule-change event.

A-FIELD-SHORTAGE-MINOR.statement: Field reader shortage and the route-completion shortfall are assumed to be a secondary/minority contributor to disputes rather than the dominant mechanism, since most disputed bills use ACTUAL reads, not ESTIMATED substitutes.

A-HANDOFF-INTEGRITY-UNKNOWN.statement: Handoffs H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL are assumed not to be the dominant corruption point, but their delivery_status and semantic_validity are recorded as UNKNOWN, so a handoff-level defect cannot yet be ruled out.

A-ACCOUNT-OVERLAP.statement: The 1,184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION AMI reads (E-12) are assumed to materially overlap by account with the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputed bills (E-01), though no direct account-level join between the two queries is in evidence.

proposal.summary: Customer Service originally asked for an AI agent to auto-answer dispute tickets and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), after dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1,180-1,260/month in Aug-Sep (E-05). Investigation reframed the problem (PD-1, now v2): of 3,025 disputed bills, 1,240 use ESTIMATED reads and 1,785 use ACTUAL reads (E-01); the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes trace to billing-import rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 with no unit scaling (E-14), rejecting valid AMI reads from firmware-v4.2 meters as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (1,184 reads, E-12) because v4.2 meters report in '0.1 m3' units compared against m3-based history (E-13). This mechanism is corroborated across three independent queries (E-15, E-16, E-17) but a critical unresolved question (VOB-R-5) about overlap with ACTUAL-read disputes forced the release decision to HOLD rather than release the advisory bill-correction and field-staffing deliverables.
key_points: Original stakeholder framing (ticket response speed, CL-01, SH-CS) was tested and rejected: dispute response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target, E-04), so the pain point is wrong bills, not slow handling (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING: REJECTED).
Tariff changes were ruled out as a cause (E-02 shows 0 logged tariff changes, corroborated by stakeholder claim E-06).

The confirmed mechanism (H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE: CONFIRMED, H-FIRMWARE-UNIT-MISMATCH: SUPPORTED) explains the 1,240 ESTIMATED-read disputes via BV-17/firmware-v4.2 unit mismatch (E-12, E-13, E-14), but has zero evidence it also explains the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputes (the stated 59% majority) — E-15 and E-17 both show the confirmed REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION account set is 100% ESTIMATED-type with none ACTUAL.

Field route completion ran at 0.88 vs a 0.95 target affecting 9,200 accounts (E-03), but only 320 accounts actually converted to estimated billing last cycle (E-09), indicating field staffing is at most a secondary contributor, not the dominant cause.

Release decision is HOLD: a critical open verification obligation, VOB-R-5, intersects the release scope (corroborate_field_route_shortfall:DA-ROUTE and recommend_bill_correction:DA-BILL) — it asks whether the 1,184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION accounts materially overlap the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills, which could cause the proposed bill-correction recommendation to miscount or mis-scope affected accounts.
No automated bill writes occurred or were proposed; any bill correction remains advisory pending manual approval by Billing Operations (SH-BILL) under constraint K-BILLWRITE.

The problem definition itself evolved: PD-1@v1 (which assumed the rule defect explained both read types) was INVALIDATED by E-12; PD-1@v2 is the current, narrower, confirmed problem definition, and several prior solution designs, work items and remedy candidates tied to v1 were correspondingly invalidated or superseded.
limitations_explained: VOB-U-ACTUAL-READ-MECHANISM remains OPEN and CRITICAL: it is unknown whether the same firmware/BV-17 mechanism (or a different one) explains the 1,785 ACTUAL-read disputed bills, which is outside the current release scope.

VOB-U-DEFECT-SCOPE-BEYOND-DISPUTED remains OPEN: it is unknown whether the BV-17/firmware-v4.2 defect also silently affects undisputed v4.2 accounts, so the full population impact is not characterized.
The DEFINE gate for this problem only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with several items deferred and tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved.

Patching/reverting billing-config rule BV-17 to add firmware-aware unit conversion, and establishing a cross-org process for ORG-AMI to notify ORG-UTIL of firmware/register-unit changes, are both identified remedies but were not executed in this contest and remain unfinished.
CRM ticket volume (M-DISPUTE-VOL) may not distinguish billing-error disputes from other dispute reasons, so it is an imprecise proxy for whether bill correctness has actually improved.
Field-staffing sizing only quantifies a secondary contributor at most: E-09 shows just 320 of the 9,200 accounts affected by the route-completion shortfall actually converted to estimated billing.

Any actual deployment of a BV-17 patch is outside the scope of this contest's execution (it requires a manual ORG-UTIL config change); the recommend_bill_correction output is advisory only and requires SH-BILL approval under K-BILLWRITE.
